key_insight: Noise-biased spin qudits can reduce dynamical decoupling overhead from quadratic to roughly linear in dimension, enabling much better preservation of nonclassical states.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical route to extend logical qubit coherence in higher-dimensional quantum hardware using DD sequences matched to the device’s noise bias.
method: Use a model d=8 qudit realized as an antimony donor nuclear spin in silicon
Apply dynamical decoupling sequences adapted to biased noise to suppress dephasing
Benchmark coherence preservation on uniform superpositions, cat states, and Haar-random states
evidence_signal: The abstract reports coherence improvements of about 5× to 10×, including a logical |+>_L lifetime of 225 ms versus 19 ms under free evolution and 85 ms with Hahn echo.
watch_item: The approach depends on having a strong and well-characterized noise bias, so performance may be less effective on hardware with more isotropic or poorly understood noise.
paper_title: Dynamical Decoupling of Nonclassical States in a Biased-Noise Spin Qudit
